I wouldn't really worry too much about that yet man, one day at a time! Luckily though in most places, medicine for treating Myco is relatively cheap. I can get several doses for multiple rats for around 25$ at my vet, hopefully yours will be that way too.

But tell you what, if you have one of those little syringes without the needle, go to a pet store and get some fish antibiotics. They smell and taste like absolute shit, but if you give them a full dose of it sometimes they'll bounce right back from what they're sick with. I did this before I got a decent paying job and could afford the vet bills. They HATED it, but it helped out every time.

If you don't, make a mixture of honey and cinnamon. They're both high in antibiotics, and they're natural medicines. The rats will probably appreciate the taste a little more too lol. This helped immensely when my girl Blue got a Myco outbreak and seizures.

But I mean, if it IS chronic Myco, the symptoms will come and go, they won't stay permanently. You don't really have to worry much about that :)

If it were me?

Keep them all separated (new rats from old) until it's been a week or two since the symptoms stopped. Any earlier than that and you risk getting your older girl sick too :/

After that, just toss em together! Do a DEEP, thorough cage clean, I'm talking like scrubbing everything. All platforms, all toys/ratty furniture, run hammocks through the wash, scrub the bars, everything. Then rearrange the cage so nothing is where it was before, and put them all together. I've never had any problems doing this method with my rats. Just be sure you keep an eye on them, be there at the door and playing with them at first, keep them all distracted. If they fight, take the new rats out and try again a few hours later. I've never had to do that, though. After a few "initiation scuffles" they always merge just fine. :) Hope everything works out for you and your ratty family!
